# #227 — Make realtime session lane creation idempotent for scoped append_session_event

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy
Labels: enhancement
Created: 2026-06-28T18:03:52Z
Updated: 2026-06-28T20:06:36Z
Closed: 2026-06-28T20:06:36Z

---

## Problem

Realtime Hermes agents can fail a scoped memory write when the Open Brain session lane does not already exist. That makes first-write behavior depend on manual lane setup or a prior successful session-start path.

For an OB-backed agent such as Nagatha, this is the wrong contract. A missing lane is normal first-write/startup state, not a user/operator error.

Observed failure pattern:

- Hermes/Nagatha attempted a scoped `append_session_event`.
- The write failed because no existing session lane existed for the scope/key.
- Fallback to an unscoped thought was considered, but that loses the Discord/platform/thread scope that makes the event useful.

This issue is intentionally narrower than #221-224. It is the immediate unlocker for Hermes-side Nagatha work in `rodaddy/rtech-hermes#276`.

## Related Work

- `rodaddy/rtech-hermes#276` needs this contract to integrate Hermes with OB realtime session lanes for Nagatha.
- #221 covers recovery WAL for interrupted realtime sessions.
- #222 covers scoped hot working sets.
- #223 covers NATS/JetStream transport foundation.
- #224 covers promotion/relegation lifecycle.

Those are related but broader. This issue only covers idempotent lane creation and first scoped append behavior.

## Required Contract

Open Brain should support one or both of these patterns:

### Option A: explicit ensure

```text
ensure_session_lane(scope) -> lane
```

Behavior:

- create the lane if missing;
- return the existing lane if present;
- be idempotent for repeated calls with the same exact scope;
- enforce namespace/auth/scope predicates;
- return enough lane metadata for the client to write scoped events.

### Option B: first-write create

```text
append_session_event(..., create_if_missing=true)
```

Behavior:

- if the lane is missing and the caller is authorized, create it and append the event;
- if the lane exists, append normally;
- if creation is denied, fail with an auth/scope error, not a generic missing-lane error.

Either option is acceptable. Supporting both is fine.

## Scope Shape

The lane scope must be exact enough for realtime agents:

```text
namespace
agent
platform/source
server/guild
channel
optional thread
session_key
```

The implementation must not spill events across agents, guilds, channels, threads, or sessions.

## Error Semantics

For failed scoped writes, return structured errors that let Hermes decide whether to spool/retry or stop.

Minimum classes:

- retryable outage/timeout/backend unavailable;
- auth or namespace denial;
- scope validation error;
- permanent unsupported operation;
- conflict/race handled by retry or idempotent return.

Do not make clients parse a generic string like "lane not found" for control flow.

## Non-Goals

- Do not implement recovery WAL here; that is #221.
- Do not implement hot working sets here; that is #222.
- Do not implement NATS transport here; that is #223.
- Do not implement promotion/relegation here; that is #224.
- Do not auto-promote scoped session events to durable/shared truth.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] There is a documented create-or-return lane operation, or `append_session_event` supports documented first-write creation.
- [ ] First scoped append for a new realtime session succeeds without manual lane pre-creation.
- [ ] Repeated ensure/first-write calls for the same exact scope are idempotent.
- [ ] Cross-scope writes are denied.
- [ ] Missing lane is no longer treated as a user/operator setup failure.
- [ ] Error responses distinguish retryable outage, auth/scope denial, validation, permanent failure, and conflict/race.
- [ ] Contract docs/schema expose the behavior so Hermes/openbrain-memory clients can rely on it.
- [ ] Tests cover:
  - first write creates lane or succeeds with `create_if_missing`;
  - existing lane append;
  - repeated ensure is safe;
  - cross-scope denial;
  - retryable failure shape;
  - auth/scope failure shape.

## Hermes/Nagatha Canary

After this lands, Hermes should be able to run this live canary from Nagatha:

```text
Remember this scoped correction for this Discord thread: GitHub issue URLs must use live gh first.
```

Pass:

- a scoped session event is written under the active Discord lane;
- if the lane did not exist, it is created automatically;
- no unscoped `log_thought` fallback is needed;
- if OB is unavailable, Hermes can identify the failure as retryable and spool/replay.

Fail:

- agent/operator must manually create the lane;
- write only lands as an unscoped thought;
- missing lane is returned as a generic unrecoverable failure.
